profile.summary: SaProt is a protein language model whose vocabulary covers structure as well as sequence. Each position is a single token that pairs the amino acid with a Foldseek structure token derived from the 3D structure, so one input string carries both. It was trained by masked language modelling on about 40 million protein sequences and structures. It is used for zero-shot variant effect prediction, for embeddings, and as a starting point for fine-tuning on supervised tasks.

summary_quotes.text: we introduce the concept of a “  s tructure-  a ware vocabulary” that integrates residue tokens with structure tokens. The structure tokens are derived by encoding the 3D structure of proteins using Foldseek.
We then propose SaProt, a large-scale general-purpose PLM trained on an extensive dataset comprising approximately 40 million protein sequences and structures.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model is an ESM-style masked language model: the 650M checkpoint has 33 layers, hidden size 1280, 20 attention heads and rotary position embeddings. The difference is the vocabulary of 446 tokens, one per pair of amino acid and Foldseek structure letter, so the string M#EvVpQpL# is read as the tokens M#, Ev, Vp, Qp and L#. A helper calls the Foldseek binary to turn a PDB or mmCIF file into the structure letters. The hash character marks a position whose structure is left out, which the developers advise for AlphaFold2 regions with pLDDT below 70.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Four checkpoints are listed: SaProt_35M_AF2 (35M parameters, 40M AF2 structures), SaProt_650M_AF2 (650M, 40M AF2 structures), SaProt_650M_PDB (650M, the same first phase plus 60K PDB structures in a second phase) and SaProt_1.3B_AFDB_OMG_NCBI (1.3B, AF2 structures plus 200M OMG_prot50 and 150M NCBI sequences filtered at 70% identity). A 35M residue-sequence-only version and an inverse folding checkpoint are also published. The README says the ProteinGym checkpoint was trained in September 2023. A result must name the checkpoint and the Hugging Face revision, and say whether structure tokens or amino acids alone were used, since the two modes behave differently.
sections.source_locator: README.md: Model checkpoints, News, ProteinGym benchmark; Hugging Face API sha fields

quotes.text: | 1.3B parameters | 40M AF2 structures + 200M OMG_prot50 + 150M NCBI (70% identity filtering)|

sections.title: Structure tokens or sequence alone
sections.body: The choice of input mode matters. The developers state that the 35M and 650M models need structure tokens for their best results: the amino acid only mode works but should be fine-tuned, and their frozen embeddings are meant for structure-aware input, not plain sequences. The 1.3B models are said to work well either way. Where a structure is predicted rather than measured, the developers report lower numbers with ESMFold structures than with AlphaFold2 structures, for example 0.455 against 0.478 Spearman on ProteinGym. These are the developers' figures and have not been reproduced by Rewire.
sections.source_locator: README.md: note at the top; AlphaFold2 vs. ESMFold

quotes.text: SaProt (35M and 650M) requires structural (SA token) input for optimal performance. Its AA-only sequence mode works but should be finetuned - its frozen embeddings work only for SA input, not AA sequences!
In contrast, SaProt-1.3B (SaProt_1.3B_AF2 & SaProt_1.3B_AFDB_OMG_NCBI) performs well with both SA tokens and AA-only sequences.

strengths.text: Structure enters as part of the token vocabulary, so one ordinary transformer handles sequence and structure without a separate structure encoder.

quotes.text: a “  s tructure-  a ware vocabulary” that integrates residue tokens with structure tokens

strengths.text: The checkpoints load through the standard transformers ESM classes, and the repository also offers loading through the esm package.

strengths.text: Code and weights are MIT, which permits commercial use.

run_guide.summary: Install the environment, load the 650M checkpoint and score a point mutation on a structure-aware sequence.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 in a conda environment, as the README's installation section sets up.
A CUDA device: the examples set device to cuda.
The Foldseek binary in the bin folder, to turn a structure file into structure tokens.
The SaProt_650M_AF2 checkpoint directory from Hugging Face. Code and weights are MIT.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaProt.git
cd SaProt
git checkout --detach e91e4858b55944523f1f8d385f7b96a0d3d34c1d
steps.explanation: The repository URL is the one the paper's abstract gives for the code. The clone and detached checkout lines are added by Rewire so the later commands match the files read at this commit.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda create -n SaProt python=3.10
conda activate SaProt

steps.title: Score a mutation
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
from model.saprot.saprot_foldseek_mutation_model import SaprotFoldseekMutationModel

config = {
    "foldseek_path": None,
    "config_path": "weights/PLMs/SaProt_650M_AF2",
    "load_pretrained": True,
}
model = SaprotFoldseekMutationModel(**config)
tokenizer = model.tokenizer

device = "cuda"
model.eval()
model.to(device)

seq = "M#EvVpQpL#VyQdYaKv" # Here "#" represents lower plDDT regions (plddt < 70)

mut_info = "V3A"
mut_value = model.predict_mut(seq, mut_info)
print(mut_value)
PY
steps.explanation: Copied from the README's Predict mutational effect block, wrapped by Rewire in a shell heredoc. Rewire replaced the placeholder /your/path/to/SaProt_650M_AF2 with the download path from the previous step.

steps.title: Build the structure-aware sequence for your own protein
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
from utils.foldseek_util import get_struc_seq
pdb_path = "example/8ac8.cif"

parsed_seqs = get_struc_seq("bin/foldseek", pdb_path, ["A"], plddt_mask=False)["A"]
seq, foldseek_seq, combined_seq = parsed_seqs

print(f"seq: {seq}")
print(f"foldseek_seq: {foldseek_seq}")
print(f"combined_seq: {combined_seq}")
PY
steps.explanation: Copied from the README's structure conversion block, wrapped by Rewire in a shell heredoc. The combined sequence is what the scoring step takes as seq. For AlphaFold2 structures the README advises plddt_mask=True.

outputs: The scoring step prints one number, the predicted effect of the substitution.
The conversion step prints the amino acid sequence, the Foldseek structure sequence and the combined structure-aware sequence.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The download step was written by Rewire from the repository and revision the sources name; the sources give no download command.
The Foldseek binary must be placed in the bin folder first, and the README points to a Google Drive link for it.
To reproduce the ProteinGym numbers, the README's own script is python scripts/mutation_zeroshot.py -c config/ProteinGym/saprot.yaml, which needs the benchmark data and is not covered here.

notes: Points for a reviewer. The 35M, 650M and 1.3B figures in the structured rows are the README's round parameter counts, converted to integers; only the 1.3B has an exact count from the Hugging Face API (1,302,899,239 tensor entries), so the others are approximate. Two further checkpoints exist that are not in the table and so have no structured row: SaProt_35M_AF2_seqOnly, a sequence-only comparison model, and SaProt_650M_AF2_inverse_folding. SaProt_1.3B_AF2 is named in the News list but has no row either, since the Model checkpoints table does not include it and its repository was not read. The preprint is the cited source here; the README states that SaProt was published in Nature Biotechnology in October 2025, which a later revision should pick up. The README's ProteinGym and ClinVar tables are the developers' own numbers.
